construct: batch stale edit recovery — the ability to reject stale-tag edits across multiple files, emit one signal per rejection, then recover by re-reading all affected files and retrying with updated tags.

input.description: The agent reads three files, then all three are externally modified (changing their content tags), then the agent attempts to edit all three using the old tags.
setup: External write to src/db.ts changes tag to #db2
External write to src/cache.ts changes tag to #ca2
External write to src/auth.ts changes tag to #au2
edit('src/db.ts', anchor='#db1', oldText='port: 3000', newText='port: 5432') is rejected
edit('src/cache.ts', anchor='#ca1', oldText='ttl: 60', newText='ttl: 300') is rejected
edit('src/auth.ts', anchor='#au1', oldText='retries: 3', newText='retries: 5') is rejected
signal store records three hashline stale-tag rejections
read_range is repeated for src/db.ts, src/cache.ts, and src/auth.ts
the same three edits are retried with updated tags and succeed

expectedBehavior: All three stale-tag edits are rejected and each rejection produces a separate signal. The agent re-reads all three files, retries with updated tags, and the final files contain the requested edits with all unrelated lines preserved.
passCondition: hashline_rejection_count >= 3 AND signal_store_event_count >= 3 AND reread_after_rejection_count >= 3 AND retry_edit_success_count == 3 AND file_content_correctness == true
failureImplication: Batch stale edits may either bypass rejection or leave the agent unable to recover with fresh tags across all affected files.
relatedPaper: AEvo Table 3: removing isolation lets 2/3 runs reward-hack.
regressionRisk: Concurrent file write logic changes may affect tag update timing across multiple files. Batch edit processing shortcuts might skip individual tag validation.
